{{Short description|none}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}}
{{Use American English|date=November 2025}}
Group I of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] took place from June 16 to 26, 2026.<ref name="match schedule">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024}}</ref> The group consisted of [[France national football team|France]], [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]], [[Iraq national football team|Iraq]], and [[Norway national football team|Norway]].

France and Norway secured their spots in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]] after two group game wins each, with France topping the group after defeating Norway in their final group game. 

Senegal finished third with a decisive victory over Iraq, allowing them to advance as one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|eight best third-place teams]]. Iraq were eliminated after losing all three of their group stage matches,<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> and they finished last in the World Cup based on goal difference.

Additionally, this edition marked Iraq’s return to the tournament after only appearing in [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]], France played its first ever World Cup on U.S. soil after having missed the [[1994 World Cup|1994]] edition<ref>{{cite web |last=Mewis |first=Joe|title= ‘Failing to reach the 1994 World Cup was one of the biggest disappointments in France’s football history. There were even fights in the dressing room’ Youri Djorkaeff on France’s 1994 failure|url= https://www.fourfourtwo.com/person/player/failing-to-reach-the-1994-world-cup-was-one-of-the-biggest-disappointments-in-frances-football-history-there-were-even-fights-in-the-dressing-room-youri-djorkaeff-on-frances-1994-failure |access-date=20 June 2026|work=[[Four Four Two]] |date=20 June 2026}}</ref> and Norway also returning since [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]].

==Standings==
{{2026 FIFA World Cup group tables|Group I}}

In the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]]:<ref name="regulations"/>
* The winner of Group I, [[France national football team|France]], advanced to play the third-place team of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group F|Group F]], [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]].
* The runner-up of Group I, [[Norway national football team|Norway]], advanced to play the runner-up of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group E|Group E]], [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]].
* The third-place team of Group I, [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]], advanced to play the winner of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group G|Group G]], [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]], as one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|eight best third-place teams]] from the group stage.

===France vs Senegal===
[[File:Aurelien Tchouameni Ibrahim Mbaye France v Senegal 16 June 2026-457.jpg|thumb|Midway in the match between France and Senegal]]
The teams had only met once prior, when Senegal defeated defending champions France 1–0 in a major [[Upset victory|upset]] at [[2002 FIFA World Cup Group A#France vs Senegal|the opening match]] of the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=France national football team: record v Senegal|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/france/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Senegal|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref>

In the first half, [[Nicolas Jackson]] hit the post with a low shot from the left that came back off French goalkeeper [[Mike Maignan]]'s leg and out for a corner. Just before half-time [[Ismaïla Sarr]] shot over the bar from six yards out after a low cross from [[Sadio Mané]] on the left.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/france-vs-senegal/report/549782|title= World Cup 2026: France 3–1 Senegal – Kylian Mbappe becomes leading scorer in Les Bleus history with stunning double|date=16 June 2026|work=Sky Sports|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>

In the second half, Mané appeared to catch [[Kylian Mbappé]] inside the box but after a VAR review no penalty was given.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c4gyr9dr4yvo|title= The VAR call that dumbfounded the world's best refs|date=16 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>
In the 66th minute, Mbappé made it 1–0 when he finished with a low right foot first time shot to the left corner from the right after a pass from [[Michael Olise]]. In the 82nd minute, Substitute [[Bradley Barcola]] ran onto a pass from [[Adrien Rabiot]] before chipping the ball over [[Édouard Mendy]] and into the net from the right to make it 2–0. In the 95th minute, Senegal pulled a goal back when substitute [[Ibrahim Mbaye]] scored with a shot from a tight angle on the right which French goalkeeper [[Mike Maignan]] got his hands to but couldn't prevent from going high into the net. A minute later, Mbappé got his second goal and France's third with a right foot shot from 30 yards out into the left of the net. 
In scoring his second goal of the game, Mbappé became the highest scorer in [[History of the France national football team|France's history]] with 58 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cze9nr5eg2xt|title= France 3 Senegal 1|date=16 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>

===Iraq vs Norway===
[[File:Iraq and Norway match 2026.jpg|thumb|Pre-match anthems of Iraq and Norway]]
The two teams had never met before. The fixture marked the return of Iraq and Norway to the World Cup finals, their first appearances since [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] and [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]] respectively.

In the 29th minute, Norway went in front when [[Erling Haaland]] slid in to score at the back post from close range after a low cross from the left by [[David Møller Wolfe]]. Iraq got an equaliser in the 39th minute when [[Aymen Hussein]] headed into the right of the net from six yards out after a cross from the left by [[Amir Al-Ammari]]. Haaland put Norway back in front four minutes later when he chased down a back-pass to Iraq goalkeeper [[Jalal Hassan]] with the ball hitting him from the goalkeeper's kick into the net.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/iraq-vs-norway/549783|title= World Cup 2026: Iraq 1-4 Norway - Erling Haaland scores twice on tournament debut as Stale Solbakken's side make winning start|date=17 June 2026|work=Sky Sports|access-date=18 June 2026}}</ref>

In the 76th minute, Norway went 3–1 in front when [[Leo Østigård]] scored with a near-post header to the net after a corner from [[Martin Odegaard]] on the right. Norway got a fourth goal in the 6th minute of added time when Haaland's looping header across goal was deflected by Aymen Hussein at the back post into his own net for an [[List of FIFA World Cup own goals|own goal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr5j6rn5ng2t|title= Iraq 1 Norway 4|date=17 June 2026|work=BBC Sport |access-date=18 June 2026}}</ref>

===France vs Iraq===
The two teams had never met before.

At 6:01&nbsp;p.m., during the halftime break, the match was interrupted due to adverse weather conditions (thunderstorm and lightning alert). The match resumed at 8:00&nbsp;p.m., and as a result, the second half was played concurrently with the first half of Norway vs Senegal in nearby New York&minus;New Jersey.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kicker.de/frankreich-gegen-irak-2026-weltmeisterschaft-5179726/ticker |title=Liveticker {{!}} Frankreich – Irak {{!}} 2. Spieltag {{!}} Weltmeisterschaft 2026 |trans-title=Live ticker {{!}} France – Iraq {{!}} Matchday 2 {{!}} 2026 World Cup |work=[[Kicker (magazine)|kicker]] |date=June 22, 2026 |access-date=June 22, 2026 |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq810n4exgvt|title= France 3 Iraq 0|date=22 June 2026|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=23 June 2026}}</ref>

With Iraq's second defeat, they now have to face Senegal in their third and final match, who also suffered two straight defeats.

===Norway vs Senegal===
The teams previously faced each other once in 2006, a friendly won 2–1 by Senegal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norway national football team: record v Senegal|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/norway/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Senegal|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref>

[[Erling Haaland]] dominated the match throughout, scoring two goals, and overwhelming the promising Senegalese team altogether, with [[Marcus Holmgren Pedersen]] having scored first in the 43rd minute. This win was enough for Norway to secure their spot to the round of 32.

===Norway vs France===
[[File:Manu Kone Jorgen Strand Larsen Maxence Lacroix France v Norway 26 June 26-146.jpg|thumb|right|During the match between Norway and France.]]
The teams had previously faced each other 16 times, most recently in 2014, a 4–0 win for France in a friendly match.<ref>{{cite web|title=France national football team: record v Norway|url=https://en.fifaranking.net/nations/fra/results/head-to-head/index.php?team=nor|website=FIFARanking.net|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref>

Before kick-off, Norway coach [[Ståle Solbakken]] decided to rest 10 of his first-team players, including [[Erling Haaland]] and [[Martin Ødegaard]], as Norway had already qualified for the knockout stage following their win against Senegal.

This marked the first time in World Cup history that Norway lost to an opponent other than [[Italy national football team|Italy]], who failed to qualify after finishing behind Norway [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group I|in their qualifying group]] and subsequently losing on penalties to [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round#Path A|play-off final]].

By scoring three goals within the first 32 minutes, [[Ousmane Dembélé]] became the second-fastest hat-trick scorer in tournament history, trailing only [[Erich Probst]] of [[Austria national football team|Austria]], who completed his in 24 minutes [[1954 FIFA World Cup Group 3#Austria vs Czechoslovakia|against Czechoslovakia]] in [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]], and the first player to score a first-half hat-trick since [[Oleg Salenko]] for [[Russia national football team|Russia]] in [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] [[1994 FIFA World Cup Group B#Russia vs Cameroon|against Cameroon]]. In addition, Dembélé became the third French player to score a hat-trick in a World Cup match, after [[Just Fontaine]] in [[1958 FIFA World Cup|1958]] and [[Kylian Mbappé]] in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]].

Following this result, France advanced as Group I winners while Norway qualified as runners-up, with the final standings heavily influenced by Norway's defensive errors and inconsistent performances.

===Senegal vs Iraq===
The two teams had never met before. This was the only match in Group I held outside of the United States.

The match was considered decisive, as both Senegal and Iraq had already lost two consecutive matches. A win for either team would secure a third-place finish in the group and a chance to proceed to the round of 32 as one of the best third-placed teams, though their qualification would still depend on the results of third-placed teams in other groups.

With this result, Senegal became the first African team to score five goals in a single FIFA World Cup match, surpassing Algeria's [[2014 FIFA World Cup Group H#South Korea vs Algeria|4–2 win]] over South Korea in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]]. This allowed Senegal to advance to the round of 32 as one of the eight best third-place teams, and the only one to progress with just three points.

Iraq were eliminated from the tournament following three consecutive defeats. This brought their overall historical record to six losses across two World Cup appearances, leaving them entirely winless since returning to the competition after a 40-year absence. 

Additionally, it marked the joint second-largest defeat suffered by an Asian team during the tournament's group stage, following Qatar's [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B#Canada vs Qatar|6–0 loss]] to Canada and tied with Uzbekistan's [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group K#Portugal vs Uzbekistan|5–0 loss]] to Portugal 3 days earlier in Houston.

<section begin="I6" />{{#invoke:football box|main
|date={{Start date|2026|6|26}}
|time=3:00&nbsp;p.m. <includeonly>[[UTC−04:00|UTC−4]]</includeonly>
|team1={{#invoke:flag|fb-rt|SEN}}
|score={{score link|2026 FIFA World Cup Group I#Senegal vs Iraq|5–0}}

==Discipline==
The team conduct ("fair play") score would have been used as a tiebreaker if the head-to-head and overall records of teams were tied. It would also be used as a tiebreaker for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|third-place ranking]] between groups if the overall records of teams were tied. The score was calculated based on yellow and red cards received by players and team officials in all group matches as follows:<ref name="regulations"/>
*yellow card: −1 point;
*indirect red card (second yellow card): −3 points;
*direct red card: −4 points;
*yellow card and direct red card: −5 points;

Only one of the above deductions could be applied to a player or team official in a single match.
